15.text: TSMC raised its full-year growth outlook again, ASML reported customer orders extending to 2030, and Broadcom is cited as Nvidia's biggest custom-chip threat, with AI revenue projected at $115 billion by 2027. Super Micro surged on AI demand, while bullish coverage favored TSMC, ASML, Arm, and Marvell.

19.text: Nvidia received about $35 billion in Blackwell chip orders from ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent, and is expanding substrate capacity 2.5x with IBIDEN, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, and Unimicron. CEO Jensen Huang said Vera Rubin will generate $40 billion per gigawatt versus $25 billion for Grace Blackwell, and reaffirmed $3–4 trillion in annual AI data-center spending by 2030.

10.text: Micron reported record quarterly earnings driven by AI memory demand, though its stock fell afterward. Articles note SK Hynix leads Nvidia's HBM supply with 50% share, while Micron shifts to contract pricing and is expected to keep growing.

8.text: Nvidia is mentioned only incidentally: these articles recommend broad ETFs (MGK, VUG, VGT, QQQ, VOO, SCHD) and note the S&P 500's top 10 holdings, mostly tech giants, now make up nearly 40% of its value.

11.text: Nebius launched public spot GPU pricing, expanded its Nvidia collaboration on secure AI agents, and borrowed $3.5 billion amid neocloud debt concerns. CoreWeave and Nebius shares fell on Musk's collapse warning and rising debt-insurance costs, though analysts see recovery.

12.text: Michael Burry has taken put options against AI stocks including Nvidia, Micron, and Palantir, betting on a dot-com-style rotation. Separately, several articles report bubble warnings from valuation indicators (CAPE above 40, Buffett indicator at 233%) and Ken Griffin, citing AI infrastructure spending.

6.text: AMD booked gigawatts of AI accelerator commitments and revenue jumped 50%, but its stock fell sharply on AI funding and data-center demand concerns. AMD’s MI450 GPUs have narrowed the performance gap with Nvidia, while analysts debate AMD’s rich valuation ahead of Nov. 3 earnings.

9.text: Nvidia shares sold off to their cheapest valuation in months despite strong revenue growth, while analysts argued the stock can still double as AI and autonomous-driving demand persists. Several articles framed pullbacks as buying opportunities ahead of next month's earnings.

17.text: Broadcom and Marvell both beat AI estimates and raised guidance, with hedge funds flipping to Broadcom in September and Marvell targeting $20B fiscal 2028 revenue. The articles frame these as non-Nvidia alternatives, barely mentioning Nvidia beyond positioning them as challengers to its dominance.

18.text: Memory chip stocks have fallen about a third from July peaks on oversupply and debt-yield worries, though Micron and Sandisk still post record margins. Nvidia's Jensen Huang disputes the bear case, saying the shortage will persist.
